title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: Why DHA matters for fetal development, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements
content:
## Introduction to Omega-3 and DHA
Omega-3 and DHA are two types of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) that are essential for the health of both mother and fetus. DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) is a particularly important type of omega-3 fatty acid for fetal brain and eye development.

## Role of DHA in Pregnancy
DHA plays a crucial role in fetal brain and eye development. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), DHA may also help reduce the risk of preterm birth and neurodevelopmental problems in infants. Additionally, DHA may help reduce the risk of postpartum depression in mothers.

## Food Sources of Omega-3 and DHA
There are many food sources rich in Omega-3 and DHA that pregnant women can incorporate into their diet. Some of these food sources include:
- Fatty fish like salmon, sardines, and anchovies
- Fortified eggs and yogurt
- Leafy green vegetables

## Fish Consumption Guidelines
Pregnant women should be mindful of their fish consumption to avoid mercury exposure. According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), pregnant women should limit their consumption of high-mercury fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel. Instead, they can consume low-mercury fish like salmon, sardines, and anchovies.

## Omega-3 and DHA Supplements
Omega-3 and DHA supplements can be a good option for pregnant women who are unable to get enough through their diet. However, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider before taking any supplements to ensure safety and efficacy. According to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), pregnant women should choose supplements that contain both DHA and EPA, and should read the label carefully to ensure that the supplement does not contain any additives or preservatives.

## Conclusion
Omega-3 and DHA are essential fatty acids for the health of both mother and fetus. Pregnant women can get these fatty acids through their diet or supplements. However, they should be mindful of their fish consumption and consult with their healthcare provider before taking any supplements. For more information on pregnancy nutrition and supplements, pregnant women can visit our [pregnancy meal planner](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner) or [read more about prenatal nutrition](/blog/prenatal-nutrition).

## When to Consult a Healthcare Provider
Pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider before taking any Omega-3 and DHA supplements if:
- They have any underlying health conditions
- They are taking any medications or supplements
- They have any allergies or sensitivities
